newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MP urges end to Ciller graft probes.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MP urges end to Ciller graft probes.

text.p: A Turkish Islamist MP close to Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Monday called for three parliamentary corruption investigations hanging over coalition ally Tansu Ciller to be dropped on a legal technicality.
Welfare Party MP Mustafa Kamalak said parliamentary commissions investigating Ciller should be disbanded because a four-month statute of limitations had elapsed.

"The constitution clearly states that the commissions should finish their work within two months. If they can't finish then, they have a fixed two months more. The four months is now over," he told Reuters.

The opposition accuses Erbakan and True Path Party (DYP) head Ciller, a pro-Western secularist, of doing a deal to clear her as part of their coalition agreement in late June under which she became deputy prime minister and foreign minister.

Separate commissions were set up in April and May this year to investigate Welfare charges that Ciller was involved in corruption in the sale of the state-run TOFAS car maker and in contract irregularities at the TEDAS electricity company.
A third investigation into her large personal wealth began in June. Government MPs form the majority on the commissions.
The main opposition vowed Ciller would be called to account. "The inquiries cannot be scrapped," Anatolian news agency quoted Motherland Party (ANAP) deputy Hayrettin Uzun as saying.
